messages.subject: Functions & variable names
parts:
Hi folks

I think I am tying myself in knots with functions, variable names and
environments.

I would like to create a function within a function to facet groups of
time series data. The first function takes a data set and melts it,
adding a new column to group series of data. The second function
calls ggplot and plots two facets, one with a line chart, the other
with an area chart. The final output would be along the lines of
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/15384925/Economic%20Indicators.pdf

I get a variety of errors as i tinker with the code suggesting that
the ggplot function cant find the right variables (no layers,
undefined columns, variables not found in the molten data etc).

Very grateful for any help

Simeon

########################
###

library(ggplot2)
data(economics)

adGraphData <- function(data,period,indicator1,indicator2) {
df <- melt(data,id=period,measure=c(indicator1,indicator2))
df$panel <- "ind1"
df[df$variable %in% indicator2,"panel"] <- "ind2"
df$panel <- factor(df$panel,levels=c("ind1","ind2"),ordered=T)
df
}

adGraph <- function(data,period,indicator1,indicator2,...){
df <-
adGraphData(data=data,period=period,indicator1=indicator1,indicator2=indicator2)
p <- ggplot(df,aes_string(period,"value"))
p + geom_line()
p + geom_line(subset=.(panel=="ind1"),aes(colour=factor(df
$variable)),size=1.2)+
geom_smooth(subset=.(panel=="ind1"),size=1)+
geom_area(subset=.(panel=="ind2"),aes(fill=factor(df
$variable)),alpha=0.6)+
scale_y_continuous("",formatter=comma)+
scale_colour_grey("Ind1") +
scale_fill_brewer("Ind2",palette="Set1")+
facet_grid(df$panel ~. ,heights=c(2,1),scales="free")

}

adGraph(economics,period="date",indicator1="unemploy",indicator2=c("psavert","uempmed"))

messages.subject: Re: Functions & variable names
parts:
Hi:

My interpretation of the original question was how to pass the value of period declared in the function call into aes_string(). My first thought was substitute(), but I couldn't figure out  the right mantra so I tried bquote() instead.

Here's my tweak on Brandon's modification:

# ---------------

adGraph <- function(data, period, indicator1, indicator2,...){

# Reshape the input data frame
df <- melt(data, id=period, measure=c(indicator1, indicator2))

df$panel <- "ind1"
   df[df$variable %in% indicator2,"panel"] <- "ind2"
   df$panel <- factor(df$panel, levels=c("ind1","ind2"), ordered=T)

# Create the plot - pass value of period into aes_string() via bquote()
p<-ggplot(df, aes_string(x = bquote(.(period)), y = "value")) + geom_line() +

geom_line(subset=.(panel=="ind1"),
                aes_string(colour="factor(variable)"), size = 1.2) +
        geom_smooth(subset=.(panel=="ind1"),size=1) +
        geom_area(subset=.(panel=="ind2"),
                  aes_string(fill="factor(variable)"), alpha=0.6) +
        scale_y_continuous("", formatter=comma) +
        scale_colour_grey("Ind1") +
        scale_fill_brewer("Ind2", palette="Set1")+
facet_grid(panel ~ . , heights=c(2,1), scales="free_y")

print(p)
   }

adGraph(data=economics, period="date", indicator1="unemploy", indicator2=c("psavert", "uempmed"))

# ------------------
AFAICT, it yields the same plot as Brandon's solution and should be a little more general.

The warning is simply to state that scale_*_brewer() uses a minimum of three and a maximum of eight colors in the palette. I'm not quite sure of what's going on in the area plot, but I haven't looked at the data frame that closely and don't have much occasion to use area plots. It appears that the bottom panel is of the contemporaneous time series of psavert (whose minimum value is negative) and uempmed. The area plot looks nice, but the shadings from pink to dark red and from light to dark blue (not to mention the little section of black at the end) isn't represented in the legend so it kind of begs the question as to what it's supposed to represent...I'm guessing overlap of one series onto the other in combination with the alpha transparency, but it's not obvious, which means some explanation is likely to be necessary if the graph goes in a report as shown.

HTH,
Dennis

library(ggplot2)
data(economics)

adGraphData <- function(data,period,indicator1,indicator2) {
   df <- melt(data,id=period,measure=c(indicator1,indicator2))
   df$panel <- "ind1"
   df[df$variable %in% indicator2,"panel"] <- "ind2"
   df$panel <- factor(df$panel,levels=c("ind1","ind2"),ordered=T)
   df
}

adGraph <- function(data,period,indicator1,indicator2,...){
   df <-
adGraphData(data=data,period=period,indicator1=indicator1,indicator2=indicator2)
   p  <- ggplot(df,aes_string(period,"value"))
   p + geom_line()
   p +  geom_line(subset=.(panel=="ind1"),aes(colour=factor(df
$variable)),size=1.2)+
        geom_smooth(subset=.(panel=="ind1"),size=1)+
        geom_area(subset=.(panel=="ind2"),aes(fill=factor(df
$variable)),alpha=0.6)+
        scale_y_continuous("",formatter=comma)+
        scale_colour_grey("Ind1") +
scale_fill_brewer("Ind2",palette="Set1")+
        facet_grid(df$panel ~. ,heights=c(2,1),scales="free")

}

adGraph(economics,period="date",indicator1="unemploy",indicator2=c("psavert","uempmed"))
